name: Tufts Blue
lede: Tufts Blue is a bright, slightly violet blue used as Tufts University's school color, a branding name rather than a pigment or dye.

sections.title: A university's blue
sections.body:
Our library traces the name to a Wikipedia list that cites Pourpre.com but gives no adoption date [1]. The library also records Bleu de France as a near-duplicate of this swatch, 1.0 units away, a French national-color name landing on almost the same blue [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[dodger-blue]], 2.8 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as more vivid [2]. [[blue-grey]] sits at 5.0, duller, [[clear-cadet-blue]] at 5.6, also duller, and [[azure]] at 5.7, more vivid and purpler [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 58, chroma 48, a bright, moderately saturated blue [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within six units of this one, over at least five percent of the canvas, in just 13 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.05 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is an anonymous *Portrait of Martin Luther* of 1529; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. The largest area of it is in a 1660 Mughal portrait of Prince Azam Shah, and Ferdinand Hodler's *Lake* of 1911 holds it across nearly a third of the canvas [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
